questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question:
The correct order of electron gain enthalpy with the negative sign where F, Cl, Br and I, having the atomic numbers 9, 17, 35, and 53 respectively, is:

1. F > Cl > Br > I

2. Cl > F > Br > I

3. Br > Cl > I > F

4. I > Br > Cl > F
questions.explanation:
Hint: Second-period element has less negative electron gain enthalpy than third-period element The electron gain enthalpy value for the given element is as follows: O = -141 kJ mol-1; S = -200 kJ mol-1; F = -328 kJ mol-1; Cl = -349 kJ mol-1 * O vs. S: Both are in Group 16. O is smaller, so you’d expect a more negative ΔH_eg, but electron repulsion in O’s smaller 2p orbitals makes it less negative (-141) than S (-200). So, O < S (less negative to more negative). * F vs. Cl: Both are in Group 17. F is smaller, but again, electron repulsion in F’s 2p orbitals reduces its ΔH_eg (-328) compared to Cl (-349). So, F < Cl. * Across Periods: Cl (Group 17) has a more negative ΔH_eg than S (Group 16), and F more negative than O, due to higher nuclear charge in halogens. * Overall Order: From least negative to most negative: O (-141) < S (-200) < F (-328) < Cl (-349).
